findings: May 8 and November 7 document the same US customer scope, eligible Link auto-enablement, supported Payment Links, Hosted Checkout and Payment Element, and merchant opt-out in Link settings under Pay later with Klarna. Link must be enabled. The transaction and shopper still have to qualify, and product visibility does not guarantee a plan or approval (old raw lines 4-16, new raw lines 5-17).

Both captures distinguish a Klarna first-use flow for an existing Link customer, involving Pay later, Continue to payment plans, identity confirmation, Klarna account creation, offered plan selection, and review and Pay, from the returning Klarna-in-Link flow, with details already saved to Link, review and Pay, and return to the merchant's success page (old raw lines 27-54, new raw lines 28-55). Link identity, Klarna identity, payment state and fulfillment are separate.

Both captures describe an issuer-authorization prerequisite and immediate net merchant credit to the Stripe account without waiting for Klarna's subsequent installment collections. This wording concerns merchant Stripe-account credit, with distinct evidence for balance settlement and bank payouts. Sandbox cards retain Visa credit 4242424242424242 for installments and unbranded debit 4687388888888881 for financing, each with any three-digit CVC and future expiration (old raw lines 18-25 and 56-58, new raw lines 19-26 and 57-59).

The mapped source retains location, surface, opt-out, UI milestones and both test fixtures, but overstates funding and automatic enablement by omitting the fee, authorization, destination and eligibility qualifications. Add the existing Link customer's identity, sandbox scope and UI-to-outcome distinction. Date the old local images and November CDN references.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Keep the May 8, 2026 scope, eligibility and Link settings toggle, two sandbox card purposes and CVC/expiry conditions, distinct first-use and repeat flows and conditioned net Stripe-account funding as dated evidence also corroborated by November. Keep the seven old local image references as May evidence. November has corresponding external URLs, with no binary or rendered comparison.

The section titled Future payments concerns Klarna collecting installments after the original purchase. The source pair does not describe a merchant-initiated saved-method payment or an off-session setup API.

The Link concept lines 34, 48 and 171 and stripe-index line 443 likewise compress confirmation, Stripe-account credit, balance settlement and payout. Keep the dated wording and scopes visible, and avoid equating these stages or claiming an instant external bank payout.

The same Link funding group doc lists lfsg_004 for Klarna, dynamic eligibility and different Charge paths for link versus card.wallet.link (raw/stripe-payments-link-link-payment-methods-2026-11-07.md:13-23,27-50). The Express Checkout Element reference lists Link and Klarna as separate available buttons (raw/stripe-payments-link-express-checkout-element-link-2026-11-07.md:5-15). Keep reciprocal surface warnings so those generic descriptions do not extend Klarna inside Link to Express Checkout, Embedded Checkout, other client flows, global standalone Klarna coverage, or a top-level Klarna payment method type. The standalone Klarna get-started reference gives eligibility and plan constraints (raw/stripe-payments-klarna-2026-11-07.md:107-115,135-143); it does not establish which plans a particular Link shopper will receive.

Clarify that new Klarna on Link means a first use by an existing Link customer, while the general Link payment methods guide separately describes signing up for Link and subsequent Link authentication (raw/stripe-payments-link-link-payment-methods-2026-11-07.md:56-77). Returning Link-stored Klarna details support a shopper-initiated review and Pay. Link or Klarna account identity, selecting a plan, prefill and success-page navigation do not prove approval or a new transaction outcome. The April 20 Checkout fulfillment guide is companion guidance for Hosted Checkout and Payment Links: check server-side Checkout Session payment_status and use webhooks for fulfillment (raw/stripe-checkout-fulfillment-2025.md:21-38,233-253). Its November canonical capture is a variant index.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/klarna, Link customers in the United States can use Klarna with Payment Links, Stripe Checkout (Hosted) and Payment Element. Turning on Link enables Klarna subject to eligibility. Merchants can unselect Pay later with Klarna in Link settings. An existing Link customer using Klarna there for the first time selects Pay later and Continue to payment plans, confirms identity, creates a Klarna account, chooses an offered plan, reviews and clicks Pay. Returning customers review Link-saved prefilled details, click Pay, and are shown returning to the merchant's success page. Both flows require separate payment-state verification. The May 8 and November 7 captures say that, after the customer's payment method issuer authorizes the Klarna payment, Stripe immediately credits the full purchase amount minus Stripe fees to the merchant's Stripe account, without waiting for Klarna's installment collection (old raw line 58 and new raw line 59). This is the Klarna on Link funding statement. The general Link integrations guide separately describes successful payments settling to Stripe balance on the card-payment timeline (raw/stripe-payments-link-link-payment-integrations-2026-11-07.md:9). Standalone Klarna separately gives standard payout timing (raw/stripe-payments-klarna-2026-11-07.md:37-39). None of those documentation statements verifies a particular authorization, capture or external payout. Sandbox cards are Visa credit 4242424242424242 for installments and unbranded debit 4687388888888881 for financing, each with a three-digit CVC and a future expiry (new raw lines 5-26 and new raw lines 28-59). These facts match May (old raw lines 4-25 and old raw lines 27-58). source-stripe-klarna-on-link.md preserves the surface and flow outline, but omits eligibility and the funding prerequisite, deduction and Stripe-account destination, and does not make the existing Link identity or sandbox scope explicit.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/link/klarna, November adds capture metadata, reformats the unchanged test table and changes seven local image references to CDN URLs. The captions, configuration, tests and payment copy are substantively unchanged (old raw lines 4-58 and new raw lines 5-59). Keep the May and November asset references dated, and correct source-stripe-klarna-on-link.md to retain merchant and session eligibility, the US Link customer and three-surface scope, and the dated funding condition. The May 8 and November 7 captures say that, after the customer's payment method issuer authorizes the Klarna payment, Stripe immediately credits the full purchase amount minus Stripe fees to the merchant's Stripe account, without waiting for Klarna's installment collection (old raw line 58 and new raw line 59). This is the Klarna on Link funding statement. The general Link integrations guide separately describes successful payments settling to Stripe balance on the card-payment timeline (raw/stripe-payments-link-link-payment-integrations-2026-11-07.md:9). Standalone Klarna separately gives standard payout timing (raw/stripe-payments-klarna-2026-11-07.md:37-39). None of those documentation statements verifies a particular authorization, capture or external payout. Add reciprocal warnings for the generic Link integration and Express Checkout button lists, which do not add a fourth Klarna-inside-Link surface, and for global standalone Klarna options. The Link payment methods reference classifies Klarna as funding source group `lfsg_004`, reported on `Charge.payment_method_details.link.funding_source_group` for Link as a payment method or `Charge.payment_method_details.card.wallet.link.funding_source_group` for a card-specific Link integration. This code classifies the underlying Link funding source. The Charge identifier and top-level payment method identity are separate (raw/stripe-payments-link-link-payment-methods-2026-11-07.md:17-38). A selected plan, sandbox card, Link-saved details or customer return does not verify issuer approval, charge, capture, settlement, fulfillment or bank payout. Companion Hosted Checkout and Payment Links fulfillment guidance verifies Checkout Session payment_status and uses webhooks (raw/stripe-checkout-fulfillment-2025.md:21-38,233-253). The guide gives no Link-specific API or SDK version requirement and does not establish recurring or off-session merchant charges.
